weather_source: NASA POWER hourly point API; MERRA-2 temperature and CERES/SYN1DEG solar, model/grid data rather than household observations
weather_attribution: NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project, funded through the NASA Earth Science Directorate Applied Science Program
weather_derivation: monthly_temperature_c = arithmetic mean of valid hourly T2M; monthly_temperature_max_c = mean of daily UTC maximum T2M; monthly GHI = sum(hourly Wh/m2)/1000/days; CDH(Ts)=sum(max(T2M-Ts,0)); cooling_days = count(UTC days with max T2M > Ts). Exact thresholds 22..30 C; interpolation between thresholds is a model approximation. Single calendar year 2024, not climatology or household AC schedule.
solar_source: European Commission Joint Research Centre PVGIS 5.3 PVcalc; PVGIS-ERA5 2005-2023
solar_attribution: PVGIS (c) European Communities, 2001-2026; public-use data with source acknowledgement

solar_system_assumptions.horizon: PVGIS DEM-calculated horizon; no site-specific obstructions
solar_system_assumptions.self_consumption: Not supplied by PVGIS. The application uses a separate explicit annual self-consumption assumption; this cache is gross generation only.

limitations: One weather year is not a typical meteorological year or a climate normal.
NASA grid-point weather is not property-measured weather; city coordinates are representative city centres.
PVGIS multi-year yield and NASA single-year heat loads have different reference periods.
PVGIS inter-year SD only represents modeled climate variability, not complete system or demand uncertainty.
All cities use the same explicitly fixed 20-degree south-facing PV system; actual roof geometry, shading and system losses can differ.
